source: Lawsen (2025) The Illusion of the Illusion of Thinking (comment on Shojaee et al.)
finding: Full text read. The function-output claim for Tower of Hanoi rests on one prompt at N=15 with four models. It reports no counts, no pass rate and no trial number. The author says the sample is too small for statistics. It is an arXiv comment (v2, 16 Jun 2025), not peer reviewed.
numbers: Prompt: 'Solve Tower of Hanoi with 15 disks. Output a Lua function that prints the solution when called.' Models: Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Claude Opus 4, o3, Gemini 2.5. Result: 'very high accuracy', under 5,000 tokens. A full move list at N=15 is 2^15-1 = 32,767 moves; at 10 tokens per move that is about 327,670 tokens, far above the 64k to 100k limits the author uses (max solvable N about 12 to 13). River Crossing is impossible for N>5 at boat size 3.
quote: Due to budget constraints, we were unable to conduct enough trials for a highly powered statistical sample.
limits: Footnote admits low power. v1 had a wrong token analysis written by an AI co-author and was revised after commenters. It tests only whether the model knows the algorithm, not whether it can execute 32k moves.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: not supported with counts and not peer reviewed. Still a useful design rule: for a long rule-bound answer, ask for a generating program and run it, instead of asking for the full list.

source: Dellibarda Varela et al. (2025) Rethinking the Illusion of Thinking
finding: Independent re-run of Hanoi and River Crossing with Gemini reasoning models. Splitting the Hanoi solution into short stages (stepwise prompting) did not remove the collapse: it still falls at about 8 disks. Two models in dialogue did worse, failing from N=4. River Crossing failures were largely unsolvable instances; on solvable ones the model solved up to 100 pairs.
numbers: Hanoi N=3 to 10, 10 trials per N, two methods (stepwise, agentic dialogue). Success rates are shown in figures only. Stepwise: clear decrease from N about 8. Dialogue: struggles from N=4. River Crossing: N=2 to 100 pairs, k=2 to 4, solvable only.
limits: One model family. Numbers are in figures. It tests shorter output horizons, not the function-output notation of Lawsen. Only 10 trials per cell.
agent_relevance: Partial contradiction of 'it is only a typing problem': even with short stages, execution of long move sequences fails near 8 disks. Pair a program-output notation with an external executor rather than trusting hand execution.

source: Khan, Madhavan, Natarajan (2025) A Comment on The Illusion of Thinking: Reframing the Reasoning Cliff as an Agentic Gap
finding: Argues the collapse is an interface limit: the models were not allowed to run code. Shows case studies where tool-enabled o4-mini and GPT-4o get further on River Crossing than the text-only cliff. Evidence is a few chat transcripts and a token-cost calculation, not a sample study.
numbers: Token argument: Hanoi needs 2^N-1 moves at about 8 tokens each; the authors put the resource cliff near N=13. Success probability decays as p^T: at p=0.999 per step the model is expected to fail near N=10; 50 percent success is lost only near N=17 for higher p. Case study: River Crossing N=20, k=4; tool-enabled o4-mini succeeded, tool-enabled GPT-4o executed a flawed plan and failed.
limits: Anecdotal, one run per case, no statistics. Industry authors, preprint.
agent_relevance: Supports giving the agent a code executor for long rule-bound state updates. A second case where notation (typed-out trace vs executable program) decides success. Evidence strength low.

source: Xu et al. (2024) LLMs and the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus: Successes, Failures, and the Importance of Object-based Representations (TMLR)
finding: Same ARC tasks, same model, only the encoding of the grid changed. A flat text grid loses object cohesion across lines. An object-based text encoding built by an external tool nearly doubled GPT-4 and removed the gap between horizontal and vertical tasks.
numbers: GPT-4 on the 50 easiest ARC tasks: 13/50 with the direct grid, 23/50 with the object-based JSON. Full ARC training set: 81/400 to 97/400. Mini-ARC: 35/149 to 45/149. 1D-ARC (one-line grids): GPT-4 reaches 50/50 on some task types; GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 also improved. Per-task gains in 1D-ARC from +20 to +96 points.
limits: GPT-4 (2023-24) and open Llama-2; no reasoning model. Prompts fixed per method. One benchmark.
agent_relevance: Best direct LLM analogue of Zhang and Norman in the set: same items, different external notation, large effect. Relevant to the ARC portfolio: give the agent an object list, not only a flat grid. Closes part of gap 1 (same items, not true isomorph).

source: Wang et al. (2024) Is A Picture Worth A Thousand Words? Delving Into Spatial Reasoning for Vision Language Models (SpatialEval, NeurIPS 2024)
finding: The same spatial questions given as text only (TQA), image only (VQA) or image plus text (VTQA). Image-only rarely beats text-only. Adding text to the image helps the VLM. Replacing the image with noise improved results. Proprietary models do well on Spatial-Grid with text or image plus text.
numbers: Four-option questions. Spatial-Grid: Llama-3 text 71.9%, Mixtral-7B 62.1% text vs LLaVA-v1.6-Mistral-7B 47.1% (15 points lower). GPT-4V gains 25.6% on Spatial-Grid from vision-only to vision plus text. GPT-4o Spatial-Grid vision plus text 0.989. Maze-Nav and Spatial-Map: most models near random with image only.
limits: 2024 models, no reasoning models. Many cells only in spider plots. Synthetic maps, mazes, grids.
agent_relevance: Rule for gap 5: where the structure is a small grid or a map with text-describable entities, text matches or beats the picture, and the picture adds little unless text is also present. Keep a text state as the primary channel.

source: Kaesberg et al. (2026) Is Visual Prompting All You Need? Studying VLM Spatial Reasoning under Progressive Visual Scaffolds (SPaRC)
finding: One puzzle (SPaRC grid path planning), planning held fixed, only the input representation changed. Adding coordinates or text symbols to the image raised accuracy a lot, and the best scaffolded image beat the text version. Most of the original gap is perception of the board, not planning.
numbers: Qwen 3.5 397B: original image 14.4%, text baseline 38.0%, image with Text Symbols 48.4% (+10.4 over text), Cell Coordinates 47.8%. Qwen 3.5 27B 8.2% to 40.0% (Cell Coordinates). Gemma 4 31B 2.2% to 26.2%. Gemma 3 27B and Mistral Small 3.2 stay below 1%. On the original board Start, End and Gap cells are found 69%, 48% and 21% of the time (65% of Gap cells called Path); with Text Symbols 100% for these. GRPO on 4B and 8B Thinking models: +3.8 and +4.6 points on scaffolded input vs near zero on the original. Prior work: SPaRC text 15.8% vs image 5.6%.
limits: One task family; scaffolds are task specific. Open-weight VLMs only. One run per cell, bootstrap intervals in an appendix.
agent_relevance: Closest thing in the set to a same-puzzle, several-notations test on current models (gap 1). The ranking image < text < image-with-symbols shows notation moves solve rate by 10 to 34 points at fixed planning load. Measure per format; do not assume.

source: Lo et al. (2026) When 2D Tasks Meet 1D Serialization: On Serialization Friction in Structured Tasks
finding: Three layout-defined tasks (matrix transpose, Game of Life, LU decomposition). The same instances were given as flat 1D text or as a rendered 2D image to models fine-tuned per condition. Text degrades sharply as size grows; the image stays high within the trained size range. Outside the training range both fall.
numbers: Transpose, matched train/eval: text 92.7% at 12x12 to 0.8% at 20x20; image stays above 90% (90.8% at 20x20). Mixed training: image 99.9, 99.8, 95.4 vs text 88.6, 74.5, 57.4 at 12, 14, 16. Game of Life: text 86.5% (4x4) to 46.6% (8x8); image above 99.7%. Mixed training: text 90.2 to 70.9, image 100 to 99.5. LU, mixed training: text 0.6, 0.3, 0.4% vs image 98.8, 93.5, 69.2%; single training on 3x3, tested at 4x4: text 15.3% vs image 88.4%. A layout-disrupted image probe is also reported.
limits: Fine-tuned small models (GLM text vs a vision-language model), so format and model capacity are mixed. Synthetic tasks. No frontier model run zero-shot.
agent_relevance: Boundary for gap 5: when the relation is positional (row-column, neighbour) and size grows, flat text fails and layout helps. For small grids text is enough (d05). Rule: layout benefit grows with size and positional dependence.

source: Huang et al. (2026) Learning to Draw ASCII Improves Spatial Reasoning in Language Models (Text2Space)
finding: Models read ASCII layouts well but draw them badly from text. Having the model write the ASCII before answering did not raise answer accuracy for any of six models. Agreement between the drawn layout and the answer marks the more reliable answers. Training on layout construction improved text-only answers and transferred to other benchmarks.
numbers: Row names reconstructed from the text (the extracted table has shifted labels). Layout construction accuracy (one turn): Qwen2.5-7B 12.5%, Llama-3-70B 42.2%, GPT-4.1 50.6%, GPT-OSS-20B 38.9%, Qwen3-235B 45.3%, Qwen3-30B 27.9%. Read-write gap 13 to 27 points. Answer accuracy text-only vs ASCII-first: Qwen2.5-7B 42.0 vs 36.7; Llama-3-70B 71.7 vs 66.9; GPT-4.1 85.8 vs 83.8; GPT-OSS-20B 93.3 vs 91.9; Qwen3-235B 84.8 vs 82.3; Qwen3-30B 75.0 vs 66.6. Accuracy on instances where ASCII and answer agree vs all: GPT-OSS-20B 97.0 vs 94.3; Qwen3-235B 95.0 vs 84.2; Llama-3-70B 87.6 vs 71.1; Qwen3-30B 88.5 vs 71.1. Agreement rate (share kept): 75.9, 67.8, 65.2, 46.1 percent. Fine-tuned Qwen3-30B-A3B: generation 29.2% to 67.9%.
limits: Table rows are garbled in text extraction; the row mapping was checked against Table 3 and the text but remains reconstructed. Spatial relation questions only. One run per cell.
agent_relevance: Gap 6. Model-drawn state is wrong more than half the time even for strong models, and writing it first does not raise accuracy. A code check on the drawn state works as a filter: agreement predicts correctness (+2.7 to +17 points on the kept answers) but 24 to 54 percent of items are dropped. Token cost not reported. Gap 10 proxy: two formats from one model disagree on a quarter to a half of items.

source: Herbst et al. (2026) Lost in Serialization: Invariance and Generalization of LLM Graph Reasoners
finding: Graph tasks (Erdos benchmark) under node relabelling, edge reordering and syntax changes. Sorted edge lists stay close to the default. Adjacency lists shift some tasks, with the worst drops on edge counting and density. Adjacency matrices often lose a lot. Larger non-fine-tuned reasoning models vary least; fine-tuned graph models vary most.
numbers: Std of accuracy over four syntax encodings (edge list text, JSON, PyG code and one more): gpt-oss-20B 5.41, gpt-oss-120B 3.45, Qwen 3B 5.98, Qwen 7B 5.86, G1-3B 9.69, G1-7B 10.51 (percentage points). G1 at temperature 0 vs 0.06 nearly identical (62.53 vs 63.21 for 3B). Matrices inflate length to O(n^2).
limits: Heat maps in figures; only some cells in text. Models: Qwen, G1 (fine-tuned), gpt-oss.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: for current models keep a sorted edge list as the default store, avoid adjacency matrices, and expect a 3 to 10 point spread from syntax alone, smaller for larger reasoning models. Put canonical sorting into the state writer.

source: Podstawski (2026) Graph Property Inference in Small Language Models: Effects of Representation and Reasoning Strategy
finding: Three 3B models estimate graph metrics from text. Adjacency-list encoding gave lower error than edge-list in most model and strategy cells, but all models stayed unreliable.
numbers: Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-4-mini, Qwen2.5-3B. NRMSE-std gain from adjacency over edge list up to 0.117 (Qwen, baseline prompt), 0.168 (Qwen, another strategy) and 0.103 (Phi). Spearman gain up to 0.114 (Llama). Best Spearman only 0.308. Some cells negative (Llama NRMSE-std -0.045).
limits: Very small models only; graph metrics, not question answering; no frontier model.
agent_relevance: With d09 and Fatemi (b15): the best list format depends on task and model (adjacency helps neighbour-heavy metrics, edge lists help counting). Gap 8 stays open for frontier models; no head-to-head incident vs adjacency vs edge vs table study was found for them.

source: Hu et al. (2026) Draw2Think: Harnessing Geometry Reasoning through Constraint Engine Interaction
finding: A GeoGebra constraint engine checks every drawing step in a propose-draw-verify loop, training-free. Gains appear where the missing resource is executable state and vanish or reverse where the baseline is already saturated. Removing the engine's query tools lowers accuracy.
numbers: Gemini 3 Flash base. Construction check on GeoGoal (N=256, 13,254 predicates): 95.94% predicate-level, 84.0% strict problem-level. Outcome gains up to +4.1% planar, +5.8% MathVerse-solid, +16.4% SolidGeo-hard Level 3. Thinking tokens fall 36% on GeoSketch and 14% on OlympiadBench. Portability on OlympiadBench N=112: baseline 100/112 correct for all three models; with engine 100 (Gemini 3 Flash), 103 (Claude Sonnet 4.6), 106 (GPT-5.4). Negative on Geo3K and PGPS9K (saturated).
limits: Authors' own harness, one main backbone; the 112-item check is small. A checker in the loop is confounded with tools and exact measuring.
agent_relevance: Supports a checker that owns the state (LLM analogue of K01) with a token cost of zero or negative when state is hard to simulate, and overhead when it is not. Gap 3: frontier models still gain from externalised state, by 0 to 6 items of 112 on a nearly saturated set.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) On the Self-Verification Limitations of LLMs on Reasoning and Planning Tasks; with Valmeekam et al. (2023) Can LLMs Really Improve by Self-critiquing Their Own Plans?
finding: GPT-4 critiquing its own answers made results worse; a sound external verifier gave large gains, and merely re-prompting with the verifier kept most of the benefit. The closest LLM test of rules checked outside versus held in the model.
numbers: 100 instances per domain, GPT-4. Standard prompting / self-critique / sound external critique (binary feedback, first-error feedback): Game of 24 5 / 3 / 36, 38; Graph Colouring 16 / 2 / 38, 37; Blocksworld 40 / 55 / 60, 87. Sampling k=25 for comparison: 42, 44, 72. Valmeekam 2023 on Blocksworld: generator only 40/100, LLM+LLM with backprompting 55/100, LLM+VAL (sound checker) 88/100; the LLM verifier was right on 61/100 plans.
limits: GPT-4 era (2023-24). It is not rules-in-prompt vs rules-in-checker on a fixed puzzle; the checker also gives repair feedback. No reasoning model tested.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 partial: an external sound check beat the model's own checking by 30 to 50 points in these domains. It does not show the human result (zero rule violations), because rules in prompt vs rules in checker were not isolated.

source: Nath et al. (2026) Representation Robustness under Executable Reasoning Constraints in LLMs for Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: 85 algebra problems, each in story, word-equation, symbolic and isomorphic-paraphrase forms, five current models. Correctness flips across equivalent forms and the isomorphic paraphrase causes regressions. A code-executing interface helps some models but shifts failures into protocol violations and execution errors, and does not remove form sensitivity.
numbers: Models: GPT-5.2-chat, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Grok 4.1 Fast, Llama 3.3 70B. Baseline vs code on shared forms: story chi2=13.14, p=0.00029; symbolic chi2=8.44, p=0.0037; word-equation chi2=2.63, p=0.105 (Bonferroni alpha 0.0167). Cramers V: story 0.073, symbolic 0.058, word-equation 0.032 (small). Representation gap (best minus worst form) is nontrivial for all models and larger for Llama under code.
limits: Accuracies are in plots; the paper itself calls the observed gaps modest. Algebra word problems, not a stateful puzzle. Deterministic decoding, one run.
agent_relevance: Nearest published isomorph-style test on current LLMs (gap 1): surface form matters, but for frontier models the effect is modest, and an executor changes the failure type rather than removing it. Expect single-digit point spreads, not Zhang and Norman sized gaps.

source: Wang et al. (2026) VisGym: Diverse, Customizable, Scalable Environments for Multimodal Agents
finding: Four symbolic tasks rendered as images or as ASCII. GPT-5 did 3 to 4 times better with ASCII on most. Gemini 2.5 Pro was mixed. Matchstick Equation went the other way because figlet-style ASCII distorts glyphs. Removing the environment's text feedback about rule violations lowered every model.
numbers: Frontier models averaged 46.6% (easy) and 26.0% (hard) success. ASCII vs image: GPT-5 often 3 to 4 times higher; Gemini 2.5 Pro two tasks no change, one up, one down. Removing text feedback (constraint violations such as hitting a wall) gave consistent drops for all models. A long unbounded history was worse than a truncated window.
quote: Several text-based symbolic tasks become substantially harder once rendered visually.
limits: Bar values are in figures only. Open-weight models near floor in both modalities. 17 environments.
agent_relevance: Rule for gap 5 on current models: for symbolic grids text or ASCII beats the picture; glyph-shaped content flips it. Also supports an environment that returns an explicit rule-violation message (gap 2).

source: Lian et al. (2025) Imagine-in-Space: SpatiaLite benchmark of spatial reasoning and efficiency in VLMs
finding: Reasoning models (o4-mini, o1, Gemini 2.5 Pro) reason mostly in language even on spatial puzzles. o4-mini is best with text-only input and gets nothing from the image; image-only drops it near zero on Wood Slide. Gemini 2.5 Pro uses vision to save tokens on easy puzzles. Reasoning models are very token-heavy on hard visual-centric tasks.
numbers: Cube Rolling: o4-mini 98.3%, o1 97.5%; o4-mini Cube Rolling Hard 94.5%, Move Box Hard 73.5%. Mental Rotation: Gemini 2.5 Pro 43% on 2 to 5 cubes, then falls. Average more than 10,000 tokens on Hard. Modality: o4-mini TQA best, VTQA no gain, VQA harms (Wood Slide near 0); Gemini 2.5 Pro image-only has a token advantage on easy items that narrows with difficulty. Open-source VLMs at chance on Rubik's Cube.
limits: Table 2 cells are garbled in extraction; the qualitative statements were checked, not every cell. Synthetic tasks.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: on native reasoning models the visual channel adds little or hurts for text-describable puzzles, and benefits are model-specific. Keep a text state as the main channel for Claude-style reasoners.

source: Xu et al. (2026) Visual Planning: Let's Think Only with Images (ICLR 2026)
finding: Planning by a sequence of images (trained with RL) beat text-only planning on FrozenLake, Maze and MiniBehavior. The text baselines, including a thinking model, scored far lower. This is a trained result, not a prompting scaffold.
numbers: Average exact match: Gemini 2.0 Flash direct 10.1, CoT 12.8; Gemini 2.5 Pro (think) 43.7; Qwen2.5-VL-7B text SFT 53.6; image planner VPFT 56.1; VPRL (images, RL) 80.6. FrozenLake EM: Gemini 2.0 Flash 21.2 and 27.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro 72.0, Qwen SFT 68.6, VPRL 91.6.
limits: Training changes the model; not a test of a scaffold. Navigation tasks that are vision-first by construction. Column mapping in the extracted table is partly garbled.
agent_relevance: Not a replication of a prompt scaffold. The visual channel can win when trained, but a native thinking model with text input (Gemini 2.5 Pro, 43.7 avg) is already close to the text-trained SFT. No help for an untrained agent.

source: Ando and Mineshima (2026) Do Diagrams Help LLMs Reason? Syllogistic Reasoning (re-analysis of the conversion cell)
finding: Full text re-read for gap 7. All conversion cases are labelled neutral, and labels are balanced at 95 items each (285 total), so label imbalance in the data is not the cause. The weak result is answer bias: GPT-4o-mini says entailment or contradiction almost always. The Sonnet conversion drop is only 2 to 3 items out of 19.
numbers: Counts reconstructed from percentages: 95 neutral, 95 entailment, 95 contradiction. Sonnet conversion NL 16/19 (84.2), Linear 13/19 (68.4), Euler 14/19 (73.7). GPT-4o-mini conversion NL 10/19, Euler 7/19. My Fisher exact test (unpaired) on these: NL vs Linear p=0.45, NL vs Euler p=0.69; mini NL vs Euler p=0.51. Sonnet neutral NL 60/95 vs Linear 46/95, p=0.057. Sonnet overall NL 241/285 vs Linear 231/285, p=0.32. GPT-4o-mini in NL: neutral 25.3 (24/95), entailment 81.1, contradiction 100.0.
limits: My p values are unpaired; the paper ran no tests, and the items are paired, so a paired test would be more sensitive. Diagrams were added beside the text, not in place of it. Two models, one run.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: not shown to be a diagram-format effect. The conversion cell (n=19) cannot carry a claim. Lower K14 to 'diagrams did not reliably help'. Neutral-case failure is a response bias that a countermodel check could target.

source: Fansher, Shah, Helie (2022) The effect of mode of presentation on Tower of Hanoi problem solving. Cognition 224:105041
finding: Human Tower of Hanoi, 4-disk and 5-disk, held in the head (mental) or shown on a computer (external). External display raised completion but cost more moves; mental solving was slower between moves and more efficient. Solving mentally first pushed people toward goal recursion on the next problem. Two experiments (undergraduates; Prolific workers).
numbers: Abstract only: no means or effect sizes in the abstract. Exp 1 undergraduates, Exp 2 Prolific workers; two problems (4-disk, 5-disk).
quote: External representations encourage speed while internal representations promote accuracy
limits: Abstract page read only (PubMed). It manipulates mode of presentation, not the rule-isomorph structure of Zhang and Norman. No effect sizes obtained.
agent_relevance: A modern human result that qualifies K01: an external display helps finishing but can lower move efficiency and strategy learning. For an agent: a checker helps legality but may reduce planning care, so keep a plan step before acting.

source: Chu, Rittle-Johnson, Fyfe (2017) Diagrams benefit symbolic problem-solving. Br J Educ Psychol
finding: Adding a diagram next to an algebra equation raised accuracy and the use of informal strategies in 61 seventh graders; the benefit did not depend on student ability or item complexity.
numbers: N=61, within-subject, matched equation vs equation-with-diagram items. No effect size in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only (Crossref abstract). Classroom study, one grade, algebra.
agent_relevance: Human counterpart to Ando and Mineshima: a diagram beside a symbolic item can help people, while it did not reliably help two LLMs. People use diagrams for informal strategies; models mostly read the text channel.

source: Borazjanizadeh et al. (2025) Visualizing Thought: reading of the table against o1-preview
finding: Re-read for gap 3. Against a native reasoning model, Visual Thinking (GPT-4o with diagrams in a search) loses on the easy domain and wins on harder ones. The gain is not gone, but it is bounded by the base model.
numbers: Blocksworld simple: Visual Thinking 90.2% (451/500) vs o1-preview 97.8% vs GPT-4o 35.5%. Blocksworld hard: o1-preview 23.65%; Visual Thinking 78% in the text, while the table shows 36 and 52 in nearby cells (unresolved). New domains: Visual Thinking beats o1-preview in all, e.g. Barman 30% vs 10%, Floor Tiles +16 points. Ablation headline cells: no diagram 58, code only 24, no beam search 62.
limits: o1-preview is a 2024 reasoner; no 2025-26 reasoning model was tested. 50 instances per domain. The table is garbled (see critique).
agent_relevance: Frontier evidence for gap 3: the diagram pipeline still beat o1-preview on hard planning but lost on the simple domain; newer reasoners were not checked. Do not assume transfer to current models.

source: Guo et al. (2025) Beyond Seeing: VisualToolBench - tool-enabled image perception, transformation and reasoning
finding: Giving frontier multimodal models image tools (crop, edit) helped GPT-5 but not Gemini 2.5 Pro, which did slightly better with no tools. Most remaining errors were visual perception.
numbers: 1,204 tasks (603 single-turn, 601 multi-turn). Best model GPT-5-think pass rate 18.68%. GPT-5 loses 11 to 14 points without tools or with a weak prompt. Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 2.7 points higher without tools.
limits: Open-ended rubric tasks on imperfect photos, not state diagrams. Tool training differs by vendor.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: the Sketchpad-style gain from tools is model-specific on current frontier models, not a general law. Measure tool-on vs tool-off for the agent's own model.

source: Zhang and Wang (2005) The effect of external representations on numeric tasks. Q J Exp Psychol A 58:817-838
finding: Same lab as Zhang and Norman. Small changes to a two-digit comparison task changed the result: with external representations people compared digits in parallel, not holistically. The authors read this as the external form changing the process, not only the memory load.
numbers: Abstract only: no numbers.
limits: Abstract only. Not independent of the 1994 lab. Not a replication of the Hanoi isomorph effect.
agent_relevance: Supports reading Zhang and Norman as 'the form of the external display changes the process used', which is what a notation change would do to a chain of thought.

source: Search record for gap 4: citation lists of Zhang and Norman 1994 (1,364 citations) and Larkin and Simon 1987 (4,188 citations) on Semantic Scholar
finding: The first 800 and 1,000 titles of the two citation lists were scanned for replication, isomorph or Hanoi work. No direct replication or failed replication of either paper turned up. Related human work: Zhang 1997 (1,107 citations, Cognitive Science 21), Zhang and Wang 2005, Fansher et al. 2022 (Hanoi mode of presentation), Chu et al. 2017. The Larkin and Simon full text could not be fetched (publisher blocks bots); the paper stays unopened.
numbers: No effect sizes found. Zhang and Norman 1994 exact means remain in figures only.
limits: The citation API returns at most the first 800 to 1,000 citations; titles only; no abstract screening. Absence of a replication is not shown, only not found.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open. Treat the Zhang and Norman isomorph effect as one lab's finding (with Zhang 1997 and Zhang and Wang) plus the older Kotovsky-Hayes-Simon isomorph work, and do not quote an effect size.
